newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada base metals shares weaken on U.S. rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Canada base metals shares weaken on U.S. rate rise.

text.p: Canadian base metals stocks eased on Tuesday in what traders said was a reaction to the widely expected rate increase in the United States.

"One of the things that does happen in markets if interest rates rise a bit, is metals prices start to ease off a bit because theoretically people stop using as much metal," said Rolie Bradley, institutional salesman at Maison Placements Canada Inc.
On the Toronto Stock Exchange, Falconbridge Ltd shares fell 1.30 to 30.45 and Alcan Aluminium dropped 1 to 49 in brisk trade. Inco lost 0.70 to 47.90.
In New York, Alcan was off 5/8 at 35-3/4, while Inco shed 1/2 to 34-7/8.
Bradley said nickel miners could also be down due to the narrowly averted strike at the flagship plant of Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group. The strike had been helping nickel prices higher.
U.S. aluminum stocks were weaker as well. On the New York Stock Exchange, Aluminum Co of America relinquished 1-5/8 to 70-3/8 and Reynolds Metals Co gave up 1-3/4 to 62-3/8.
